This artifact shows that AUROC was measured on an outcome that was **already at ceiling before the lesion**, so it could not have fallen in either direction. Re-expressed on an outcome **with headroom** -- TPR at a fixed, low false-positive rate -- the same activations reveal a **site dissociation**:\n\n- **EARLY / prompt site** (reads the harmful *request*): the operating point is flat under the full lesion (`dTPR@1%FPR` +0.0007) -- recognition of the harmful request survives, as iteration 1 claimed.\n- **LATE / response site** (reads the model's *continuation*): the same statistic falls substantially (`dTPR@1%FPR` -0.1439) while AUROC there moves only -0.0137 -- about a **10.5x larger movement in the operating point than in the summary statistic that was reported**.\n\nThis notebook also reproduces the TOST equivalence verdicts per lesion strength and the restricted-labelled-budget (`k` in `{16, 32, 64}`) AUROC ordering, which tracks safety tuning rather than raw capability: `Base ~ NonSafetyFT << Instruct < SafeRL`.\n\n## Run invariant\n\n> The commissioned comparison and any metric built from it must read **ACTIVATIONS or WEIGHTS** of a single model. **Logit-only and text-only readouts are baselines, never the result.** Every row of every table carries a `READOUT_CLASS` field; no summary sentence may name a `BASELINE_ONLY` row as the answer.\n\nThis is a **mechanistic-interpretability study of WHERE SAFETY LIVES** -- recognition of harm versus execution of a refusal -- not a jailbreak or attack-success-rate study. No attack-success rate appears as an outcome anywhere below; behavioural columns, where they appear, are only the ground truth an internal (activation-level) readout is validated against.\n\n**What this notebook does.** Because the raw activations/`.npz` files are not shipped with this demo, the notebook works from `mini_demo_data.json`: a 96-row curated subset of the artifact's own `results/m1_recognition_headroom.csv`, one row per (lineage x lesion-strength x window) arm plus paired lesion contrasts. It re-derives the M1 headline numbers from those stored rows and checks each one against the artifact's own `metrics_agg_reference`, printing MATCH/MISMATCH -- exactly the claim-checking style `eval.py` itself uses.", "cell_id": "cell-0"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "import subprocess, sys\ndef _pip(*a): subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '-q', *a])\n\n# numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy -- pre-installed on Colab, install locally to match\n# Colab's exact versions. Nothing else is required: this notebook only does table\n# arithmetic over an already-computed JSON table, no model loading.\nif 'google.colab' not in sys.modules:\n    _pip('numpy==2.0.2', 'pandas==2.2.2', 'matplotlib==3.10.0', 'scipy==1.16.3')", "cell_id": "72ebc4f7", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "import json\nimport math\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom scipy import stats as sps\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt", "cell_id": "7df9c5d1", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "GITHUB_DATA_URL = \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-f8532e-safety-only-checks-output-when-warned/main/round-2/evaluation-1/demo/mini_demo_data.json\"\n\n\ndef load_data():\n    \"\"\"Try the published copy on GitHub first, then the local file next to this notebook.\"\"\"\n    import urllib.request\n\n    try:\n        with urllib.request.urlopen(GITHUB_DATA_URL, timeout=10) as resp:\n            return json.loads(resp.read().decode(\"utf-8\"))\n    except Exception:\n        local_path = Path(\"mini_demo_data.json\")\n        if local_path.exists():\n            return json.loads(local_path.read_text())\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\n            f\"Could not fetch {GITHUB_DATA_URL} and no local mini_demo_data.json was found.\"\n        )", "cell_id": "c24d62e1", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "data = load_data()\nprint(f\"loaded dataset '{data['dataset']}' ({len(data['rows'])} rows, {len(data['columns'])} columns)\")\nprint(data[\"description\"])\nprint(\"source file in the original artifact:\", data[\"source_file\"])\nprint(\"prereg_sha256:\", data[\"prereg_sha256\"])", "cell_id": "7f82726b", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## Config\n\nEvery tunable this notebook uses, named up front. The pre-registration (`evalkit/prereg.py`) and the M1 module (`evalkit/m1_recognition.py`) fix most of these; the ones that control run *cost* (`N_BOOT`) are set here to the smallest value that still produces a real answer, with the original full-artifact value noted alongside. If the run stays fast at that minimum, the comment shows what to scale it up to.", "cell_id": "eee25666"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "# Qwen3-4B lineages: base, instruct, SafeRL (safe-completion), non-safety fine-tune control\nLINEAGES = (\"L1\", \"L2\", \"L3\", \"L4\")\n\n# read sites: LATE = response/continuation site, EARLY = prompt/request site\n# (evalkit/m1_recognition.py: WINDOWS, PRIMARY_WINDOW)\nWINDOWS = (\"LATE\", \"EARLY\")\nPRIMARY_WINDOW = \"LATE\"  # response site: where an EXECUTION account predicts the lesion should bite\n\n# lesion (activation-steering ablation) strengths swept in the artifact\nALPHAS = (\"0.00\", \"0.25\", \"0.50\", \"0.75\", \"1.00\")\nALPHA_BASE = \"0.00\"   # unlesioned control\nALPHA_FULL = \"1.00\"   # fully lesioned\n\n# TOST equivalence margin, TPR units (evalkit/prereg.py: M1_equivalence_margin_tpr_units)\nMARGIN = 0.05\n\n# bootstrap draws for the R5 power-sentence SE (evalkit/stats.py: BOOT_DRAWS = 10_000).\n# Set to the minimum that still gives a stable, non-degenerate SE; scale up if fast.\nN_BOOT = 200  # original full value: 10_000\n\n# absolute tolerance for MATCH vs MISMATCH when checking a recomputed number\n# against metrics_agg_reference (mirrors eval.py's claim-diff tolerance style)\nCLAIM_TOLERANCE = 0.01\n\n# restricted labelled-budget sizes (evalkit/prereg.py: M1_restricted_budgets_k)\nBUDGETS = (16, 32, 64)\n\n# evalkit/stats.py bootstrap seed, reused here for reproducibility\nRANDOM_SEED = 20260921\n\nprint(f\"LINEAGES={LINEAGES}  WINDOWS={WINDOWS}  PRIMARY_WINDOW={PRIMARY_WINDOW!r}\")\nprint(f\"ALPHAS={ALPHAS}  MARGIN={MARGIN}  N_BOOT={N_BOOT}  CLAIM_TOLERANCE={CLAIM_TOLERANCE}\")\nprint(f\"BUDGETS={BUDGETS}  RANDOM_SEED={RANDOM_SEED}\")", "cell_id": "05b3ccef", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 1. Parse the table, split the two sources, check the run invariant\n\nEvery row of `mini_demo_data.json[\"rows\"]` arrived as CSV strings. We coerce the numeric columns to floats (an empty string becomes `NaN`, exactly like a blank CSV cell) and split the table by its `source` prefix into:\n\n- **(a) Lane B** per-item band activations -- the arms that carry a lesion strength (`alpha`) and a read site (`window`); this is where the site dissociation lives.\n- **(b) Lane A** per-item cell projections -- a second, independent activation source reported beside Lane B.\n\nThen we check the run invariant directly: every row must carry `READOUT_CLASS`, and we count how many rows are *result-eligible* (`activation`/`weight`) versus *baseline-only* (`logit`/`text`/`metadata`).", "cell_id": "35efe170"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "df = pd.DataFrame(data[\"rows\"])\n\nNUMERIC_COLS = [\n    \"n_pos\", \"n_neg\", \"auroc_recomputed\", \"tpr@1fpr_point\", \"smallest_resolvable_step\",\n    \"tpr@5fpr_point\", \"mde_80pct\", \"auroc_k16_mean\", \"auroc_k32_mean\", \"auroc_k64_mean\",\n    \"delta_tpr@1fpr\", \"equivalence_margin\", \"equivalence_margin_achieved\",\n    \"p_tost\", \"p_two_sided\", \"auroc_stored\", \"splithalf_stored\",\n    \"cos_rcontent_rrequest_stored\",\n]\nfor c in NUMERIC_COLS:\n    df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors=\"coerce\")\ndf[\"BASELINE_ONLY\"] = df[\"BASELINE_ONLY\"].map({\"True\": True, \"False\": False})\ndf[\"DESCRIPTIVE\"] = df[\"DESCRIPTIVE\"].map({\"True\": True, \"False\": False})\n\nlane_b = df[df[\"source\"].str.startswith(\"(a)\")].reset_index(drop=True)  # LANE_B per-item band activations\nlane_a = df[df[\"source\"].str.startswith(\"(b)\")].reset_index(drop=True)  # LANE_A per-item cell projections\n\nprint(f\"{len(df)} rows total: {len(lane_b)} from (a) Lane B, {len(lane_a)} from (b) Lane A\")\n\nhas_readout_class = df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].notna().all() and (df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"] != \"\").all()\nprint(\"READOUT_CLASS present on every row:\", has_readout_class)\nassert has_readout_class, \"run invariant violated: a table row is missing READOUT_CLASS\"\nprint(df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].value_counts())\n\nn_result_eligible = int(df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].isin([\"activation\", \"weight\"]).sum())\nn_baseline_only = int(df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].isin([\"logit\", \"text\", \"metadata\"]).sum())\nprint(f\"result-eligible rows (activation/weight): {n_result_eligible}\")\nprint(f\"baseline-only rows (logit/text/metadata):  {n_baseline_only}\")", "cell_id": "fa49f197", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 2. Per-arm AUROC and TPR@1%FPR by lesion strength: the ceiling story\n\nFor each read site (`window`) and lesion strength (`alpha`), average `auroc_recomputed`, `tpr@1fpr_point`, `tpr@5fpr_point` and `auroc_k16_mean` over the four lineages. This is the same aggregation `eval.py`'s report builds (\"the de-saturation, in one table\"): AUROC is already close to its ceiling at `alpha=0.00` (unlesioned) in both windows, so a probe scored only on AUROC has almost no room left to register damage. TPR at a fixed, low FPR is the outcome with headroom.", "cell_id": "2e075531"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "# evalkit/m1_recognition.py source (a) rows, as plain dicts -- kept close to the\n# original report code, which iterates row dicts rather than the DataFrame\nlane_b_recs = lane_b.to_dict(\"records\")\n\nhead_rows = []\nfor win in WINDOWS:\n    for a in ALPHAS:\n        sel = [r for r in lane_b_recs\n               if r[\"window\"] == win and str(r[\"alpha\"]) == a\n               and np.isfinite(r[\"tpr@1fpr_point\"])]\n        if not sel:\n            continue\n\n        def _mean(col: str) -> float:\n            vals = np.array([r[col] for r in sel], dtype=float)\n            vals = vals[np.isfinite(vals)]\n            return round(float(vals.mean()), 4) if vals.size else float(\"nan\")\n\n        head_rows.append({\n            \"window\": win, \"lesion_alpha\": a, \"n_lineages\": len(sel),\n            \"mean_AUROC\": _mean(\"auroc_recomputed\"),\n            \"mean_TPR@1%FPR\": _mean(\"tpr@1fpr_point\"),\n            \"mean_TPR@5%FPR\": _mean(\"tpr@5fpr_point\"),\n            \"mean_AUROC_k16\": _mean(\"auroc_k16_mean\"),\n        })\n\nhead_df = pd.DataFrame(head_rows)\nprint(\"The de-saturation, in one table (AUROC is the outcome iteration 1 reported;\")\nprint(\"TPR at a fixed FPR is the SAME activations read with headroom):\\n\")\nprint(head_df.to_string(index=False))", "cell_id": "03b3fc99", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 3. The site dissociation: EARLY vs LATE, unlesioned to fully lesioned\n\n`_site(window, col)` is `eval.py`'s own function (`_emit_eval_out._site`), copied verbatim: the mean at `alpha=1.00` minus the mean at `alpha=0.00`, averaged over the four lineages, at one read site. We compute it for `auroc_recomputed` and `tpr@1fpr_point` at both windows, then the ratio `|dTPR@1%FPR| / |dAUROC|` at the response site -- the \"how many times further the operating point moved than the summary statistic\" number. Each recomputed value is then checked against `metrics_agg_reference` with `CLAIM_TOLERANCE`, printing `MATCH`/`MISMATCH` exactly the way `eval.py`'s M8 provenance ledger checks a claimed number against a recomputed one.", "cell_id": "508f9f63"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "def _site(window: str, col: str) -> float:\n    \"\"\"alpha=1.00 minus alpha=0.00, averaged over lineages, at one read site.\n\n    Copied verbatim from eval.py's _emit_eval_out (file paths -> lane_b_recs).\n    \"\"\"\n    def mean_at(a: str) -> float:\n        vals = [r[col] for r in lane_b_recs if r[\"window\"] == window and str(r[\"alpha\"]) == a]\n        vals = [v for v in vals if np.isfinite(v)]\n        return float(np.mean(vals)) if vals else float(\"nan\")\n    return mean_at(ALPHA_FULL) - mean_at(ALPHA_BASE)\n\n\nsite = {}\nfor win in WINDOWS:\n    d_auroc = _site(win, \"auroc_recomputed\")\n    d_tpr1 = _site(win, \"tpr@1fpr_point\")\n    ratio = abs(d_tpr1) / abs(d_auroc) if d_auroc else float(\"nan\")\n    site[win] = {\"d_auroc\": d_auroc, \"d_tpr1\": d_tpr1, \"ratio_tpr1_over_auroc\": ratio}\n    label = (\"EARLY = prompt site (the harmful REQUEST)\" if win == \"EARLY\"\n             else \"LATE = response site (the CONTINUATION)\")\n    print(f\"{label}\\n  d mean AUROC={d_auroc:+.4f}  d mean TPR@1%FPR={d_tpr1:+.4f}  \"\n          f\"ratio |dTPR1%|/|dAUROC|={ratio:.1f}x\\n\")\n\nref = data[\"metrics_agg_reference\"]\n\n\ndef check(label: str, recomputed: float, ref_key: str, tol: float = CLAIM_TOLERANCE) -> str:\n    claimed = ref[ref_key]\n    verdict = \"MATCH\" if abs(recomputed - claimed) <= tol else \"MISMATCH\"\n    print(f\"[{verdict}] {label}: recomputed={recomputed:.4f}  claimed(reference)={claimed:.4f}  \"\n          f\"|delta|={abs(recomputed - claimed):.4f}\")\n    return verdict\n\n\nprint(\"Claim check against metrics_agg_reference (tolerance = \"\n      f\"{CLAIM_TOLERANCE}):\\n\")\ncheck(\"EARLY delta AUROC (full lesion)\", site[\"EARLY\"][\"d_auroc\"],\n      \"m1_site_EARLY_delta_auroc_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"EARLY delta TPR@1%FPR (full lesion)\", site[\"EARLY\"][\"d_tpr1\"],\n      \"m1_site_EARLY_delta_tpr1_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"LATE delta AUROC (full lesion)\", site[\"LATE\"][\"d_auroc\"],\n      \"m1_site_LATE_delta_auroc_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"LATE delta TPR@1%FPR (full lesion)\", site[\"LATE\"][\"d_tpr1\"],\n      \"m1_site_LATE_delta_tpr1_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"LATE TPR@1%FPR / AUROC movement ratio\", site[\"LATE\"][\"ratio_tpr1_over_auroc\"],\n      \"m1_site_LATE_tpr1_over_auroc_movement_ratio\")", "cell_id": "cbe69f18", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 4. Equivalence: stored TOST verdicts, then the copied `tost` re-run\n\nFirst we tabulate the `equivalence_verdict` `eval.py` already stored on every `M1.R4` lesion-pair row (`LESION_PAIRS` in `evalkit/m1_recognition.py`: `0.00->1.00`, and `0.00->{0.25,0.50,0.75}`), by lesion strength and window, and check the whole-table `EQUIVALENT`/`NOT_EQUIVALENT` counts against `metrics_agg_reference`.\n\nThen, to show the equivalence machinery itself rather than only its stored output, `TostResult` and `tost()` are copied **verbatim** from `evalkit/stats.py` (the only change: the local variable `df` is renamed `df_` because `df` is this notebook's DataFrame), and re-run on the four-lineage vector of full-lesion (`alpha 0.00 -> 1.00`) `delta_tpr@1fpr` values at the **primary window**, at the pre-registered `MARGIN`. `power_sentence`/`paired_bootstrap_se` (also copied verbatim, parameterised by `N_BOOT`/`RANDOM_SEED`) attach the R5 power sentence to that same vector.", "cell_id": "9fa4399c"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "# evalkit/m1_recognition.py: LESION_PAIRS\nLESION_PAIRS = [(a, \"1.00\") for a in (\"0.00\",)] + [(\"0.00\", a) for a in (\"0.25\", \"0.50\", \"0.75\")]\n\nr4 = lane_b[lane_b[\"metric\"] == \"M1.R4\"].copy()\nverdict_by_step = (r4.groupby([\"alpha\", \"window\"])[\"equivalence_verdict\"]\n                     .value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0))\nprint(\"Stored TOST verdict per lesion strength and window \"\n      f\"(LESION_PAIRS={LESION_PAIRS}):\\n\")\nprint(verdict_by_step)\n\nn_equiv = int((df[\"equivalence_verdict\"] == \"EQUIVALENT\").sum())\nn_not_equiv = int((df[\"equivalence_verdict\"] == \"NOT_EQUIVALENT\").sum())\nprint(f\"\\nwhole table: {n_equiv} EQUIVALENT, {n_not_equiv} NOT_EQUIVALENT\")\ncheck(\"n EQUIVALENT verdicts (whole table)\", float(n_equiv), \"m1_n_equivalent_verdicts\")\ncheck(\"n NOT_EQUIVALENT verdicts (whole table)\", float(n_not_equiv), \"m1_n_not_equivalent_verdicts\")", "cell_id": "ad5df2cf", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict\n\n\n# --- copied verbatim from evalkit/stats.py -------------------------------- #\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass TostResult:\n    verdict: str\n    diff: float\n    se: float\n    margin: float\n    p_lower: float\n    p_upper: float\n    p_tost: float\n    ci90_low: float\n    ci90_high: float\n    achieved_margin: float\n    n: int\n\n    def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n        return asdict(self)\n\n\ndef tost(diffs: np.ndarray, margin: float, *, alpha: float = 0.05) -> TostResult:\n    \"\"\"Two-one-sided-tests equivalence on a paired difference.\n\n    Returns EQUIVALENT only when the whole 1-2*alpha interval lies inside\n    (-margin, +margin). NOT_EQUIVALENT means the difference is itself\n    significantly non-zero; INCONCLUSIVE -- a real and expected verdict at these\n    sample sizes -- means neither, and is never to be reported as EQUIVALENT.\n    \"\"\"\n    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\n    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\n    n = d.size\n    nan = float(\"nan\")\n    if n < 2:\n        return TostResult(\"INCONCLUSIVE_N_TOO_SMALL\", float(d.mean()) if n else nan,\n                          nan, margin, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, n)\n    mean = float(d.mean())\n    se = float(d.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\n    if se == 0.0:\n        verdict = \"EQUIVALENT\" if abs(mean) < margin else \"NOT_EQUIVALENT\"\n        return TostResult(verdict, mean, 0.0, margin, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, mean, mean,\n                          abs(mean), n)\n    df_ = n - 1  # renamed from `df` -- that name is this notebook's DataFrame\n    t_lo = (mean + margin) / se\n    t_hi = (mean - margin) / se\n    p_lower = float(sps.t.sf(t_lo, df_))      # H0: diff <= -margin\n    p_upper = float(sps.t.cdf(t_hi, df_))     # H0: diff >= +margin\n    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)\n    crit = sps.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df_)\n    lo, hi = mean - crit * se, mean + crit * se\n    p_two = float(2 * sps.t.sf(abs(mean) / se, df_))\n\n    if p_tost < alpha:\n        verdict = \"EQUIVALENT\"\n    elif p_two < alpha:\n        verdict = \"NOT_EQUIVALENT\"\n    else:\n        verdict = \"INCONCLUSIVE\"\n    # smallest margin at which this data would have read EQUIVALENT\n    achieved = float(abs(mean) + crit * se)\n    return TostResult(verdict, mean, se, margin, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost,\n                      float(lo), float(hi), achieved, n)\n\n\ndef paired_bootstrap_se(diffs: np.ndarray, *, draws: int = N_BOOT,\n                        seed: int = RANDOM_SEED) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Bootstrap SE of the mean paired difference, used to invert R5's power sentence.\"\"\"\n    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\n    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\n    if d.size < 2:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    idx = rng.integers(0, d.size, size=(draws, d.size))\n    return float(np.std(d[idx].mean(axis=1), ddof=1))\n\n\ndef power_sentence(diffs: np.ndarray, *, label: str, power: float = 0.80,\n                   alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"R5. Invert the paired bootstrap SE into the effect detectable at 80% power.\"\"\"\n    se = paired_bootstrap_se(diffs)\n    n = int(np.isfinite(np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)).sum())\n    if not np.isfinite(se) or se == 0.0:\n        why = \"n<2\" if n < 2 else \"bootstrap SE is exactly zero (degenerate outcome)\"\n        return (f\"with this outcome and n = {n}, no detectable effect is \"\n                f\"computable: {why}\"), float(\"nan\")\n    mde = float((sps.norm.ppf(1 - alpha / 2) + sps.norm.ppf(power)) * se)\n    return (f\"with this outcome and n = {n}, a degradation of {mde:.4f} \"\n            f\"{label} would have been detected at power 0.80\"), mde\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\nprimary_deltas = [r[\"delta_tpr@1fpr\"] for r in lane_b_recs\n                  if r[\"metric\"] == \"M1.R4\" and r[\"window\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW\n                  and r[\"alpha\"] == f\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\"]\nprint(f\"{PRIMARY_WINDOW} (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: \"\n      f\"{[round(v, 4) for v in primary_deltas]}\")\n\nt = tost(np.array(primary_deltas), MARGIN)\nprint(f\"\\ntost(margin={MARGIN}): verdict={t.verdict}  mean_diff={t.diff:.4f}  \"\n      f\"90% CI=[{t.ci90_low:.4f}, {t.ci90_high:.4f}]  p_tost={t.p_tost:.4g}  n={t.n}\")\n\nsent, mde = power_sentence(np.array(primary_deltas), label=\"TPR units\")\nprint(f\"\\n{sent}\")\n\ncheck(\"mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows)\",\n      float(np.mean([r[\"delta_tpr@1fpr\"] for r in lane_b_recs\n                     if r[\"metric\"] == \"M1.R4\"\n                     and r[\"alpha\"] == f\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\"])),\n      \"m1_mean_delta_tpr_at_full_lesion\")", "cell_id": "5eac6eab", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 5. Restricted-budget few-prompt axis: does the ordering track safety tuning?\n\nFor each lineage's **unlesioned** (`alpha=0.00`) primary-window arm, read off the mean AUROC of a probe fit on only `k` label-stratified items, for `k` in `BUDGETS`. This is the commissioned few-prompt axis (`evalkit/m1_recognition.py: restricted_budget_auroc`), de-saturating along *supervision* rather than along the lesion. The ordering at `k=16` is checked against `metrics_agg_reference`: it should track SAFETY TUNING (`Base ~ NonSafetyFT << Instruct < SafeRL`), not raw capability -- `L1` base and `L4` the non-safety fine-tune are close together and far below `L2` instruct and `L3` SafeRL.", "cell_id": "9b02db86"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "LINEAGE_LABELS = {\"L1\": \"Base\", \"L2\": \"Instruct\", \"L3\": \"SafeRL\", \"L4\": \"NonSafetyFT\"}\n\nk_rows = []\nfor lin in LINEAGES:\n    sel = lane_b[(lane_b[\"metric\"] == \"M1\") & (lane_b[\"lineage\"] == lin) &\n                 (lane_b[\"alpha\"] == ALPHA_BASE) & (lane_b[\"window\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW)]\n    if sel.empty:\n        continue\n    row = sel.iloc[0]\n    rec = {\"lineage\": lin, \"label\": LINEAGE_LABELS[lin]}\n    for k in BUDGETS:\n        rec[f\"auroc_k{k}\"] = row[f\"auroc_k{k}_mean\"]\n    k_rows.append(rec)\nk_df = pd.DataFrame(k_rows)\nprint(f\"Restricted-budget AUROC, unlesioned ({PRIMARY_WINDOW} window):\\n\")\nprint(k_df.to_string(index=False))\n\nK16_REF_KEYS = {\n    \"L1\": \"m1_k16_auroc_base_unlesioned\",\n    \"L2\": \"m1_k16_auroc_instruct_unlesioned\",\n    \"L3\": \"m1_k16_auroc_safetyrl_unlesioned\",\n    \"L4\": \"m1_k16_auroc_nonsafety_ft_unlesioned\",\n}\nprint(f\"\\nClaim check at k=16 against metrics_agg_reference:\\n\")\nfor lin in LINEAGES:\n    recomputed = float(k_df.loc[k_df[\"lineage\"] == lin, \"auroc_k16\"].iloc[0])\n    check(f\"k=16 AUROC unlesioned {lin} ({LINEAGE_LABELS[lin]})\", recomputed, K16_REF_KEYS[lin])\n\nordered = k_df.sort_values(\"auroc_k16\")\nprint(\"\\nk=16 AUROC ordering (low to high): \" +\n      \" < \".join(f\"{r.label} {r.auroc_k16:.3f}\" for r in ordered.itertuples()))", "cell_id": "6c55bd49", "language": "python"}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 6. Summary table and figure\n\nA single readable summary table, then a two-panel figure: (a) AUROC and TPR@1%FPR versus lesion strength, for both read sites -- AUROC is nearly flat while TPR@1%FPR at the LATE site drops; (b) the restricted-budget (`k=16`) AUROC bar per lineage, showing the safety-tuning ordering.", "cell_id": "925ac861"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "print(\"=\" * 78)\nprint(\"SUMMARY: the de-saturation, in one table\")\nprint(\"=\" * 78)\nprint(head_df.to_string(index=False))\nprint()\nprint(\"Change from unlesioned to fully lesioned, averaged over lineages, per read site:\")\nsummary_moves = pd.DataFrame([\n    {\"read_site\": (\"EARLY = prompt site\" if w == \"EARLY\" else \"LATE = response site\"),\n     \"d_mean_AUROC\": site[w][\"d_auroc\"], \"d_mean_TPR@1%FPR\": site[w][\"d_tpr1\"],\n     \"ratio |dTPR1%|/|dAUROC|\": site[w][\"ratio_tpr1_over_auroc\"]}\n    for w in WINDOWS\n])\nprint(summary_moves.to_string(index=False))\nprint()\nprint(\"Restricted-budget (k=16) AUROC, unlesioned, per lineage:\")\nprint(k_df[[\"lineage\", \"label\", \"auroc_k16\"]].to_string(index=False))\n\nfig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))\n\ncolors = {\"EARLY\": \"#1f77b4\", \"LATE\": \"#d62728\"}\nax = axes[0]\nfor win in WINDOWS:\n    sub = head_df[head_df[\"window\"] == win].copy()\n    sub[\"a\"] = sub[\"lesion_alpha\"].astype(float)\n    sub = sub.sort_values(\"a\")\n    ax.plot(sub[\"a\"], sub[\"mean_AUROC\"], marker=\"o\", color=colors[win],\n            linestyle=\"-\", label=f\"AUROC ({win})\")\n    ax.plot(sub[\"a\"], sub[\"mean_TPR@1%FPR\"], marker=\"s\", color=colors[win],\n            linestyle=\"--\", label=f\"TPR@1%FPR ({win})\")\nax.set_xlabel(\"lesion strength (alpha)\")\nax.set_ylabel(\"value\")\nax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)\nax.set_title(\"AUROC saturates; TPR@1%FPR moves\\nonly at the response (LATE) site\")\nax.legend(fontsize=8, loc=\"lower left\")\nax.grid(alpha=0.3)\n\nax2 = axes[1]\nbar_colors = [\"#888888\", \"#2ca02c\", \"#1f77b4\", \"#999933\"]\nax2.bar(k_df[\"label\"], k_df[\"auroc_k16\"], color=bar_colors[: len(k_df)])\nax2.axhline(0.5, color=\"black\", linewidth=0.8, linestyle=\":\", label=\"chance (0.5)\")\nax2.set_ylabel(\"AUROC (k=16 restricted-budget probe)\")\nax2.set_title(\"Restricted-budget AUROC (k=16),\\nunlesioned -- tracks safety tuning\")\nax2.set_ylim(0, 1.0)\nax2.grid(axis=\"y\", alpha=0.3)\nax2.legend(fontsize=8)\n\nfig.suptitle(\"M1 -- Recognition with headroom: site dissociation and restricted-budget ordering\")\nfig.tight_layout()\nplt.show()", "cell_id": "9db70790", "language": "python"}]}}

{"stdout": "# Re-checking the numbers we already have\n\nA **zero-GPU, zero-API, zero-download re-adjudication** of iteration 1's three lanes,\ncomputed only from files already on disk. It runs no forward pass, downloads no\ncheckpoint, and spends nothing on judging. Its outputs are tables, not findings about\nnew data.\n\nThe scientific deliverable is iteration 1's premise re-expressed on an outcome **with\nheadroom**. Iteration 1's headline recognition outcome read AUROC 1.000 in the\nunperturbed control, so \"the representation survives the lesion\" was never falsifiable\nin either direction. It is restated here as TPR at 1% FPR, as restricted-labelled-budget\nAUROC, and as a two-one-sided-test equivalence verdict per parent-child pair, each with\nan explicit power sentence. Around it sit eight reporting repairs, all re-analysis of\nstored numbers rather than missing experiments.\n\n## The run invariant, enforced as a column\n\n> The commissioned comparison and any metric built from it must read **activations or\n> weights of a single model**. Logit-only and text-only readouts are baselines, never\n> the result.\n\nEvery row of every table carries a mandatory `READOUT_CLASS` in\n`{activation, weight, logit, text, metadata}`. Rows tagged `activation` or `weight` are\nRESULT-ELIGIBLE. Rows tagged `logit`, `text` or `metadata` print in the same table under\na permanent `BASELINE_ONLY` flag, and no summary sentence names one as the study's\nanswer. `evalkit/selfcheck.py` **rejects** a table that omits the column and rejects\nprose that names a baseline-class readout as the answer; its verdict is in\n`results/selfcheck.json`.\n\nThis is a mechanistic-interpretability study of *where safety lives* — recognition of\nharm versus execution of a refusal. Nothing here is framed as jailbreak evaluation or\nattack selection; no attack-success rate is an outcome in any table, and behavioural\ncolumns appear only as the ground truth an internal readout is validated against.\n\n## How to run\n\n```bash\n./install.sh                    # uv venv + requirements\n.venv/bin/python eval.py        # everything (~10 min, 2 CPU, no GPU)\n.venv/bin/python eval.py --smoke     # one lineage, no restricted-budget sweep (~1 min)\n.venv/bin/python eval.py --reuse-m1  # reuse results/m1_cache.json (~25 s)\n./finalize.sh                        # schema validation, mini/preview variants, size check\n```\n\nM1's restricted-budget sweep (12,000 probe fits) is the only slow step and dominates the\nruntime; it is cached to `results/m1_cache.json`, so iterating on the report costs seconds.\nSet `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` — on a 2-core box that roughly halves the sweep.\n\nThe pre-registration is written and SHA-256'd **before the first number is computed**\n(`results/prereg_eval.json`, hash in `results/prereg_eval.sha256` and in every output).\n\n## What each metric does\n\n| module | metric | READOUT_CLASS | what it settles |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `evalkit/m0_assets.py` | **M0** asset and recomputability ledger | metadata | Opens every file before any claim is made about it. We coerce the numeric columns to floats (an empty string becomes `NaN`, exactly like a blank CSV cell) and split the table by its `source` prefix into:\n\n- **(a) Lane B** per-item band activations -- the arms that carry a lesion strength (`alpha`) and a read site (`window`); this is where the site dissociation lives.\n- **(b) Lane A** per-item cell projections -- a second, independent activation source reported beside Lane B.\n\nThen we check the run invariant directly: every row must carry `READOUT_CLASS`, and we count how many rows are *result-eligible* (`activation`/`weight`) versus *baseline-only* (`logit`/`text`/`metadata`).", "cell_id": "35efe170"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "df = pd.DataFrame(data[\"rows\"])\n\nNUMERIC_COLS = [\n    \"n_pos\", \"n_neg\", \"auroc_recomputed\", \"tpr@1fpr_point\", \"smallest_resolvable_step\",\n    \"tpr@5fpr_point\", \"mde_80pct\", \"auroc_k16_mean\", \"auroc_k32_mean\", \"auroc_k64_mean\",\n    \"delta_tpr@1fpr\", \"equivalence_margin\", \"equivalence_margin_achieved\",\n    \"p_tost\", \"p_two_sided\", \"auroc_stored\", \"splithalf_stored\",\n    \"cos_rcontent_rrequest_stored\",\n]\nfor c in NUMERIC_COLS:\n    df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors=\"coerce\")\ndf[\"BASELINE_ONLY\"] = df[\"BASELINE_ONLY\"].map({\"True\": True, \"False\": False})\ndf[\"DESCRIPTIVE\"] = df[\"DESCRIPTIVE\"].map({\"True\": True, \"False\": False})\n\nlane_b = df[df[\"source\"].str.startswith(\"(a)\")].reset_index(drop=True)  # LANE_B per-item band activations\nlane_a = df[df[\"source\"].str.startswith(\"(b)\")].reset_index(drop=True)  # LANE_A per-item cell projections\n\nprint(f\"{len(df)} rows total: {len(lane_b)} from (a) Lane B, {len(lane_a)} from (b) Lane A\")\n\nhas_readout_class = df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].notna().all() and (df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"] != \"\").all()\nprint(\"READOUT_CLASS present on every row:\", has_readout_class)\nassert has_readout_class, \"run invariant violated: a table row is missing READOUT_CLASS\"\nprint(df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].value_counts())\n\nn_result_eligible = int(df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].isin([\"activation\", \"weight\"]).sum())\nn_baseline_only = int(df[\"READOUT_CLASS\"].isin([\"logit\", \"text\", \"metadata\"]).sum())\nprint(f\"result-eligible rows (activation/weight): {n_result_eligible}\")\nprint(f\"baseline-only rows (logit/text/metadata):  {n_baseline_only}\")", "execution_count": 6, "cell_id": "fa49f197", "language": "python", "outputs": [{"output_type": "stream", "text": "96 rows total: 75 from (a) Lane B, 21 from (b) Lane A\nREADOUT_CLASS present on every row: True\nREADOUT_CLASS\nactivation    96\nName: count, dtype: int64\nresult-eligible rows (activation/weight): 96\nbaseline-only rows (logit/text/metadata):  0\n"}]}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 2. The site dissociation: EARLY vs LATE, unlesioned to fully lesioned\n\n`_site(window, col)` is `eval.py`'s own function (`_emit_eval_out._site`), copied verbatim: the mean at `alpha=1.00` minus the mean at `alpha=0.00`, averaged over the four lineages, at one read site. We compute it for `auroc_recomputed` and `tpr@1fpr_point` at both windows, then the ratio `|dTPR@1%FPR| / |dAUROC|` at the response site -- the \"how many times further the operating point moved than the summary statistic\" number. Each recomputed value is then checked against `metrics_agg_reference` with `CLAIM_TOLERANCE`, printing `MATCH`/`MISMATCH` exactly the way `eval.py`'s M8 provenance ledger checks a claimed number against a recomputed one.", "cell_id": "508f9f63"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "def _site(window: str, col: str) -> float:\n    \"\"\"alpha=1.00 minus alpha=0.00, averaged over lineages, at one read site.\n\n    Copied verbatim from eval.py's _emit_eval_out (file paths -> lane_b_recs).\n    \"\"\"\n    def mean_at(a: str) -> float:\n        vals = [r[col] for r in lane_b_recs if r[\"window\"] == window and str(r[\"alpha\"]) == a]\n        vals = [v for v in vals if np.isfinite(v)]\n        return float(np.mean(vals)) if vals else float(\"nan\")\n    return mean_at(ALPHA_FULL) - mean_at(ALPHA_BASE)\n\n\nsite = {}\nfor win in WINDOWS:\n    d_auroc = _site(win, \"auroc_recomputed\")\n    d_tpr1 = _site(win, \"tpr@1fpr_point\")\n    ratio = abs(d_tpr1) / abs(d_auroc) if d_auroc else float(\"nan\")\n    site[win] = {\"d_auroc\": d_auroc, \"d_tpr1\": d_tpr1, \"ratio_tpr1_over_auroc\": ratio}\n    label = (\"EARLY = prompt site (the harmful REQUEST)\" if win == \"EARLY\"\n             else \"LATE = response site (the CONTINUATION)\")\n    print(f\"{label}\\n  d mean AUROC={d_auroc:+.4f}  d mean TPR@1%FPR={d_tpr1:+.4f}  \"\n          f\"ratio |dTPR1%|/|dAUROC|={ratio:.1f}x\\n\")\n\nref = data[\"metrics_agg_reference\"]\n\n\ndef check(label: str, recomputed: float, ref_key: str, tol: float = CLAIM_TOLERANCE) -> str:\n    claimed = ref[ref_key]\n    verdict = \"MATCH\" if abs(recomputed - claimed) <= tol else \"MISMATCH\"\n    print(f\"[{verdict}] {label}: recomputed={recomputed:.4f}  claimed(reference)={claimed:.4f}  \"\n          f\"|delta|={abs(recomputed - claimed):.4f}\")\n    return verdict\n\n\nprint(\"Claim check against metrics_agg_reference (tolerance = \"\n      f\"{CLAIM_TOLERANCE}):\\n\")\ncheck(\"EARLY delta \"m1_site_EARLY_delta_tpr1_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"LATE delta AUROC (full lesion)\", site[\"LATE\"][\"d_auroc\"],\n      \"m1_site_LATE_delta_auroc_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"LATE delta TPR@1%FPR (full lesion)\", site[\"LATE\"][\"d_tpr1\"],\n      \"m1_site_LATE_delta_tpr1_full_lesion\")\ncheck(\"LATE TPR@1%FPR / AUROC movement ratio\", site[\"LATE\"][\"ratio_tpr1_over_auroc\"],\n `metrics_agg_reference`.\n\nThen, to show the equivalence machinery itself rather than only its stored output, `TostResult` and `tost()` are copied **verbatim** from `evalkit/stats.py` (the only \"0.50\", \"0.75\")]\n\nr4 = lane_b[lane_b[\"metric\"] == \"M1.R4\"].copy()\nverdict_by_step = (r4.groupby([\"alpha\", \"window\"])[\"equivalence_verdict\"]\n (LESION_PAIRS=[('0.00', '1.00'), ('0.00', '0.25'), ('0.00', '0.50'), ('0.00', '0.75')]):\n\nequivalence_verdict  EQUIVALENT  INCONCLUSIVE  NOT_EQUIVALENT\nalpha      window EQUIVALENT, 15 NOT_EQUIVALENT\n[MATCH] n EQUIVALENT verdicts (whole table): recomputed=18.0000  claimed(reference)=18.0000  |delta|=0.0000\n[MATCH] n NOT_EQUIVALENT verdicts (whole table): recomputed=15.0000  claimed(reference)=15.0000  |delta|=0.0000\n"}, {"output_type": "execute_result", "text": "'MATCH'"}]}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict\n\n\n# --- copied verbatim from evalkit/stats.py -------------------------------- #\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass TostResult:\n    verdict: str\n    diff: float\n    se: float\n    margin: float\n    p_lower: float\n    p_upper: float\n    p_tost: float\n    ci90_low: float\n    ci90_high: float\n    achieved_margin: float\n    n: int\n\n    def as_dict(self) -> dict:\n        return asdict(self)\n\n\ndef tost(diffs: np.ndarray, margin: float, *, alpha: float = 0.05) -> TostResult:\n    \"\"\"Two-one-sided-tests equivalence on a paired difference.\n\n    Returns EQUIVALENT only when the whole 1-2*alpha interval lies inside\n    (-margin, +margin). NOT_EQUIVALENT means the difference is itself\n    significantly non-zero; INCONCLUSIVE -- a real and expected verdict at these\n    sample sizes -- means neither, and is never to be reported as EQUIVALENT.\n    \"\"\"\n    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\n    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\n    n = d.size\n    nan = float(\"nan\")\n    if n < 2:\n        return TostResult(\"INCONCLUSIVE_N_TOO_SMALL\", float(d.mean()) if n else nan,\n                          nan, margin, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, n)\n    mean = float(d.mean())\n    se = float(d.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\n    if se == 0.0:\n        verdict = \"EQUIVALENT\" if abs(mean) < margin else \"NOT_EQUIVALENT\"\n        return TostResult(verdict, mean, 0.0, margin, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, mean, mean,\n                          abs(mean), n)\n    df_ = n - 1  # renamed from `df` -- that name is this notebook's DataFrame\n    t_lo = (mean + margin) / se\n    t_hi = (mean - margin) / se\n    p_lower = float(sps.t.sf(t_lo, df_))      # H0: diff <= -margin\n    p_upper = float(sps.t.cdf(t_hi, df_))     # H0: diff >= +margin\n    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)\n    crit = sps.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df_)\n    lo, hi = mean - crit * se, mean + crit * se\n    p_two = float(2 * sps.t.sf(abs(mean) / se, df_))\n\n    if p_tost < alpha:\n        verdict = \"EQUIVALENT\"\n    elif p_two < alpha:\n        verdict = \"NOT_EQUIVALENT\"\n    else:\n        verdict = \"INCONCLUSIVE\"\n    # smallest margin at which this data would have read EQUIVALENT\n    achieved = float(abs(mean) + crit * se)\n    return TostResult(verdict, mean, se, margin, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost,\n                      float(lo), float(hi), achieved, n)\n\n\ndef paired_bootstrap_se(diffs: np.ndarray, *, draws: int = N_BOOT,\n                        seed: int = RANDOM_SEED) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Bootstrap SE of the mean paired difference, used to invert R5's power sentence.\"\"\"\n    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\n    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\n    if d.size < 2:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    idx = rng.integers(0, d.size, size=(draws, d.size))\n    return float(np.std(d[idx].mean(axis=1), ddof=1))\n\n\ndef power_sentence(diffs: np.ndarray, *, label: str, power: float = 0.80,\n                   alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"R5. Invert the paired bootstrap SE into the effect detectable at 80% power.\"\"\"\n    se = paired_bootstrap_se(diffs)\n    n = int(np.isfinite(np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)).sum())\n    if not np.isfinite(se) or se == 0.0:\n        why = \"n<2\" if n < 2 else \"bootstrap SE is exactly zero (degenerate outcome)\"\n        return (f\"with this outcome and n = {n}, no detectable effect is \"\n                f\"computable: {why}\"), float(\"nan\")\n    mde = float((sps.norm.ppf(1 - alpha / 2) + sps.norm.ppf(power)) * se)\n    return (f\"with this outcome and n = {n}, a degradation of {mde:.4f} \"\n            f\"{label} would have been detected at power 0.80\"), mde\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\nprimary_deltas = [r[\"delta_tpr@1fpr\"] for r in lane_b_recs\n                  if r[\"metric\"] == \"M1.R4\" and r[\"window\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW\n                  and r[\"alpha\"] == f\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\"]\nprint(f\"{PRIMARY_WINDOW} (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: \"\n      f\"{[round(v, 4) for v in primary_deltas]}\")\n\nt = tost(np.array(primary_deltas), MARGIN)\nprint(f\"\\ntost(margin={MARGIN}): verdict={t.verdict}  mean_diff={t.diff:.4f}  \"\n      f\"90% CI=[{t.ci90_low:.4f}, {t.ci90_high:.4f}]  p_tost={t.p_tost:.4g}  n={t.n}\")\n\nsent, mde = power_sentence(np.array(primary_deltas), label=\"TPR units\")\nprint(f\"\\n{sent}\")\n\ncheck(\"mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows)\",\n      float(np.mean([r[\"delta_tpr@1fpr\"] for r in lane_b_recs\n                     if r[\"metric\"] == \"M1.R4\"\n                     and r[\"alpha\"] == f\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\"])),\n      \"m1_mean_delta_tpr_at_full_lesion\")", "execution_count": 10, "cell_id": "5eac6eab", "language": "python", "outputs": [{"output_type": "stream", "text": "LATE (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: [-0.0833, -0.1849, -0.138, -0.1693]\n\ntost(margin=0.05): verdict=NOT_EQUIVALENT  mean_diff=-0.1439  90% CI=[-0.1966, -0.0911]  p_tost=0.9876  n=4\n\nwith this outcome and n = 4, a degradation of 0.0533 TPR units would have been detected at power 0.80\n[MATCH] mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows): recomputed=-0.0716  claimed(reference)=-0.0716  |delta|=0.0000\n"}, {"output_type": "execute_result", "text": "'MATCH'"}]}, {"cellType": "markdown", "source": "## 5. Restricted-budget few-prompt axis: does the ordering track safety tuning?\n\nFor each lineage's **unlesioned** (`alpha=0.00`) primary-window arm, read off the mean AUROC of a probe fit on only `k` label-stratified items, for `k` in `BUDGETS`. This is the commissioned few-prompt axis (`evalkit/m1_recognition.py: restricted_budget_auroc`), de-saturating along *supervision* rather than along the lesion. The ordering at `k=16` is checked against `metrics_agg_reference`: it should track SAFETY TUNING (`Base ~ NonSafetyFT << Instruct < SafeRL`), not raw capability -- `L1` base and `L4` the non-safety fine-tune are close together and far below `L2` instruct and `L3` SafeRL.", "cell_id": "9b02db86"}, {"cellType": "code", "source": "LINEAGE_LABELS = {\"L1\": \"Base\", \"L2\": \"Instruct\", \"L3\":        rec[f\"auroc_k{k}\"] = row[f\"auroc_k{k}_mean\"]\n    k_rows.append(rec)\nk_df = pd.DataFrame(k_rows)\nprint(f\"Restricted-budget AUROC, unlesioned ({PRIMARY_WINDOW} TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows): recomputed=-0.0716  claimed(reference)=-0.0716  |delta|=0.0000\\n\"\n     ]\n    },\n    {\n     \"data\": {\n      \"text/plain\": [\n       \"'MATCH'\"\n      ]\n     },\n     \"execution_count\": 10,\n     \"metadata\": {},\n     \"output_type\": \"execute_result\"\n    }\n   ],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# --- copied verbatim from evalkit/stats.py -------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"@dataclass(frozen=True)\\n\",\n    \"class TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    verdict: str\\n\",\n    \"    diff: float\\n\",\n    \"    se: float\\n\",\n    \"    margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_low: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_high: float\\n\",\n    \"    achieved_margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    n: int\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    def as_dict(self) -> dict:\\n\",\n    \"        return asdict(self)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def tost(diffs: np.ndarray, margin: float, *, alpha: float = 0.05) -> TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Two-one-sided-tests equivalence on a paired difference.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    Returns EQUIVALENT only when the whole 1-2*alpha interval lies inside\\n\",\n    \"    (-margin, +margin). NOT_EQUIVALENT means the difference is itself\\n\",\n    \"    significantly non-zero; INCONCLUSIVE -- a real and expected verdict at these\\n\",\n    \"    sample sizes -- means neither, and is never to be reported as EQUIVALENT.\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    n = d.size\\n\",\n    \"    nan = float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    if n < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(\\\"INCONCLUSIVE_N_TOO_SMALL\\\", float(d.mean()) if n else nan,\\n\",\n    \"                          nan, margin, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, n)\\n\",\n    \"    mean = float(d.mean())\\n\",\n    \"    se = float(d.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\\n\",\n    \"    if se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\" if abs(mean) < margin else \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(verdict, mean, 0.0, margin, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, mean, mean,\\n\",\n    \"                          abs(mean), n)\\n\",\n    \"    df_ = n - 1  # renamed from `df` -- that name is this notebook's DataFrame\\n\",\n    \"    t_lo = (mean + margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    t_hi = (mean - margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower = float(sps.t.sf(t_lo, df_))      # H0: diff <= -margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper = float(sps.t.cdf(t_hi, df_))     # H0: diff >= +margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)\\n\",\n    \"    crit = sps.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df_)\\n\",\n    \"    lo, hi = mean - crit * se, mean + crit * se\\n\",\n    \"    p_two = float(2 * sps.t.sf(abs(mean) / se, df_))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    if p_tost < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    elif p_two < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    else:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"INCONCLUSIVE\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    # smallest margin at which this data would have read EQUIVALENT\\n\",\n    \"    achieved = float(abs(mean) + crit * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return TostResult(verdict, mean, se, margin, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost,\\n\",\n    \"                      float(lo), float(hi), achieved, n)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def paired_bootstrap_se(diffs: np.ndarray, *, draws: int = N_BOOT,\\n\",\n    \"                        seed: int = RANDOM_SEED) -> float:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Bootstrap SE of the mean paired difference, used to invert R5's power sentence.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    if d.size < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\\n\",\n    \"    idx = rng.integers(0, d.size, size=(draws, d.size))\\n\",\n    \"    return float(np.std(d[idx].mean(axis=1), ddof=1))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def power_sentence(diffs: np.ndarray, *, label: str, power: float = 0.80,\\n\",\n    \"                   alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[str, float]:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"R5. Invert the paired bootstrap SE into the effect detectable at 80% power.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    se = paired_bootstrap_se(diffs)\\n\",\n    \"    n = int(np.isfinite(np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)).sum())\\n\",\n    \"    if not np.isfinite(se) or se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        why = \\\"n<2\\\" if n < 2 else \\\"bootstrap SE is exactly zero (degenerate outcome)\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, no detectable effect is \\\"\\n\",\n    \"                f\\\"computable: {why}\\\"), float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    mde = float((sps.norm.ppf(1 - alpha / 2) + sps.norm.ppf(power)) * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, a degradation of {mde:.4f} \\\"\\n\",\n    \"            f\\\"{label} would have been detected at power 0.80\\\"), mde\\n\",\n    \"# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"primary_deltas = [r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                  if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\" and r[\\\"window\\\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW\\n\",\n    \"                  and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"]\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"{PRIMARY_WINDOW} (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"{[round(v, 4) for v in primary_deltas]}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"t = tost(np.array(primary_deltas), MARGIN)\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\ntost(margin={MARGIN}): verdict={t.verdict}  mean_diff={t.diff:.4f}  \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"90% CI=[{t.ci90_low:.4f}, {t.ci90_high:.4f}]  p_tost={t.p_tost:.4g}  n={t.n}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"sent, mde = power_sentence(np.array(primary_deltas), label=\\\"TPR units\\\")\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\n{sent}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"check(\\\"mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows)\\\",\\n\",\n    \"      float(np.mean([r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                     if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\"\\n\",\n    \"                     and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"])),\\n\",\n    \"      \\\"m1_mean_delta_tpr_at_full_lesion\\\")\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"id\": \"9b02db86\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"## 5. Restricted-budget few-prompt axis: does the ordering track safety tuning?\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"For each lineage's **unlesioned** (`alpha=0.00`) primary-window arm, read off the mean AUROC of a probe fit on only `k` label-stratified items, for `k` in `BUDGETS`. This is the commissioned few-prompt axis (`evalkit/m1_recognition.py: restricted_budget_auroc`), de-saturating along *supervision* rather than along the lesion. {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"id\": \"942c861e\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"# Re-checking the numbers we already have: M1 recognition-with-headroom\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"This notebook is a Colab-runnable demo of the **evaluation artifact** `gen_art_evaluation_1` (\\\"Re-checking the numbers we already have\\\"), a **zero-GPU, zero-API re-adjudication** of a mechanistic-interpretability safety study on the **Qwen3-4B** lineage family: `L1` base, `L2` instruct, `L3` SafeRL (safe-completion), and `L4` a non-safety fine-tune used as a load-bearing control.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"Iteration 1 of that study reported that a harm-recognition probe's AUROC survives a representation *lesion* (an activation-steering ablation applied at strength `alpha` in `[0.00, 1.00]`) almost perfectly (~0.95-0.98 AUROC throughout). This artifact shows that AUROC was measured on an outcome that was **already at ceiling before the lesion**, so it could not have fallen in either direction. Re-expressed on an outcome **with headroom** -- TPR at a fixed, low false-positive rate -- the same activations reveal a **site dissociation**:\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"- **EARLY / prompt site** (reads the harmful *request*): the operating point is flat under the full lesion (`dTPR@1%FPR` +0.0007) -- recognition of the harmful request survives, as iteration 1 claimed.\\n\",\n    \"- **LATE / response site** (reads the model's *continuation*): the same statistic falls substantially (`dTPR@1%FPR` -0.1439) while AUROC there moves only -0.0137 -- about a **10.5x larger movement in the operating point than in the summary statistic that was reported**.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"This notebook also reproduces the TOST equivalence verdicts per lesion strength and the restricted-labelled-budget (`k` in `{16, 32, 64}`) AUROC ordering, which tracks safety tuning rather than raw capability: `Base ~ NonSafetyFT << Instruct < SafeRL`.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"## Run invariant\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"> The commissioned comparison and any metric built from it must read **ACTIVATIONS or WEIGHTS** of a single model. **Logit-only and text-only readouts are baselines, never the result.** Every row of every table carries a `READOUT_CLASS` field; no summary sentence may name a `BASELINE_ONLY` row as the answer.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"This is a **mechanistic-interpretability study of WHERE SAFETY LIVES** -- recognition of harm versus execution of a refusal -- not a jailbreak or attack-success-rate study. No attack-success rate appears as an outcome anywhere below; behavioural columns, where they appear, are only the ground truth an internal (activation-level) readout is validated against.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"**What this notebook does.** Because the raw activations/`.npz` files are not shipped with this demo, the notebook works from `mini_demo_data.json`: a 96-row curated subset of the artifact's own `results/m1_recognition_headroom.csv`, one row per (lineage x lesion-strength x window) arm plus paired lesion contrasts. \"'MATCH'\"\n      ]\n     },\n     \"execution_count\": 10,\n     \"metadata\": {},\n     \"output_type\": \"execute_result\"\n    }\n   ],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# --- copied verbatim from evalkit/stats.py -------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"@dataclass(frozen=True)\\n\",\n    \"class TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    verdict: str\\n\",\n    \"    diff: float\\n\",\n    \"    se: float\\n\",\n    \"    margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_low: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_high: float\\n\",\n    \"    achieved_margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    n: int\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    def as_dict(self) -> dict:\\n\",\n    \"        return asdict(self)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def tost(diffs: np.ndarray, margin: float, *, alpha: float = 0.05) -> TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Two-one-sided-tests equivalence on a paired difference.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    Returns EQUIVALENT only when the whole 1-2*alpha interval lies inside\\n\",\n    \"    (-margin, +margin). NOT_EQUIVALENT means the difference is itself\\n\",\n    \"    significantly non-zero; INCONCLUSIVE -- a real and expected verdict at these\\n\",\n    \"    sample sizes -- means neither, and is never to be reported as EQUIVALENT.\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    n = d.size\\n\",\n    \"    nan = float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    if n < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(\\\"INCONCLUSIVE_N_TOO_SMALL\\\", float(d.mean()) if n else nan,\\n\",\n    \"                          nan, margin, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, n)\\n\",\n    \"    mean = float(d.mean())\\n\",\n    \"    se = float(d.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\\n\",\n    \"    if se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\" if abs(mean) < margin else \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(verdict, mean, 0.0, margin, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, mean, mean,\\n\",\n    \"                          abs(mean), n)\\n\",\n    \"    df_ = n - 1  # renamed from `df` -- that name is this notebook's DataFrame\\n\",\n    \"    t_lo = (mean + margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    t_hi = (mean - margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower = float(sps.t.sf(t_lo, df_))      # H0: diff <= -margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper = float(sps.t.cdf(t_hi, df_))     # H0: diff >= +margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)\\n\",\n    \"    crit = sps.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df_)\\n\",\n    \"    lo, hi = mean - crit * se, mean + crit * se\\n\",\n    \"    p_two = float(2 * sps.t.sf(abs(mean) / se, df_))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    if p_tost < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    elif p_two < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    else:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"INCONCLUSIVE\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    # smallest margin at which this data would have read EQUIVALENT\\n\",\n    \"    achieved = float(abs(mean) + crit * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return TostResult(verdict, mean, se, margin, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost,\\n\",\n    \"                      float(lo), float(hi), achieved, n)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def paired_bootstrap_se(diffs: np.ndarray, *, draws: int = N_BOOT,\\n\",\n    \"                        seed: int = RANDOM_SEED) -> float:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Bootstrap SE of the mean paired difference, used to invert R5's power sentence.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    if d.size < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\\n\",\n    \"    idx = rng.integers(0, d.size, size=(draws, d.size))\\n\",\n    \"    return float(np.std(d[idx].mean(axis=1), ddof=1))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def power_sentence(diffs: np.ndarray, *, label: str, power: float = 0.80,\\n\",\n    \"                   alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[str, float]:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"R5. Invert the paired bootstrap SE into the effect detectable at 80% power.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    se = paired_bootstrap_se(diffs)\\n\",\n    \"    n = int(np.isfinite(np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)).sum())\\n\",\n    \"    if not np.isfinite(se) or se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        why = \\\"n<2\\\" if n < 2 else \\\"bootstrap SE is exactly zero (degenerate outcome)\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, no detectable effect is \\\"\\n\",\n    \"                f\\\"computable: {why}\\\"), float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    mde = float((sps.norm.ppf(1 - alpha / 2) + sps.norm.ppf(power)) * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, a degradation of {mde:.4f} \\\"\\n\",\n    \"            f\\\"{label} would have been detected at power 0.80\\\"), mde\\n\",\n    \"# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"primary_deltas = [r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                  if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\" and r[\\\"window\\\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW\\n\",\n    \"                  and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"]\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"{PRIMARY_WINDOW} (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"{[round(v, 4) for v in primary_deltas]}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"t = tost(np.array(primary_deltas), MARGIN)\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\ntost(margin={MARGIN}): verdict={t.verdict}  mean_diff={t.diff:.4f}  \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"90% CI=[{t.ci90_low:.4f}, {t.ci90_high:.4f}]  p_tost={t.p_tost:.4g}  n={t.n}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"sent, mde = power_sentence(np.array(primary_deltas), label=\\\"TPR units\\\")\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\n{sent}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"check(\\\"mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows)\\\",\\n\",\n    \"      float(np.mean([r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                     if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\"\\n\",\n    \"                     and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"])),\\n\",\n    \"      \\\"m1_mean_delta_tpr_at_full_lesion\\\")\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"id\": \"9b02db86\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"## 5. asdict\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# --- copied verbatim from evalkit/stats.py -------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"@dataclass(frozen=True)\\n\",\n    \"class TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    verdict: str\\n\",\n    \"    diff: float\\n\",\n    \"    se: float\\n\",\n    \"    margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_low: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_high: float\\n\",\n    \"    achieved_margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    n: int\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    def as_dict(self) -> dict:\\n\",\n    \"        return asdict(self)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def tost(diffs: np.ndarray, margin: float, *, alpha: float = 0.05) -> TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Two-one-sided-tests equivalence on a paired difference.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    Returns EQUIVALENT only when the whole 1-2*alpha interval lies inside\\n\",\n    \"    (-margin, +margin). NOT_EQUIVALENT means the difference is itself\\n\",\n    \"    significantly non-zero; INCONCLUSIVE -- a real and expected verdict at these\\n\",\n    \"    sample sizes -- means neither, and is never to be reported as EQUIVALENT.\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    n = d.size\\n\",\n    \"    nan = float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    if n < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(\\\"INCONCLUSIVE_N_TOO_SMALL\\\", float(d.mean()) if n else nan,\\n\",\n    \"                          nan, margin, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, n)\\n\",\n    \"    mean = float(d.mean())\\n\",\n    \"    se = float(d.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\\n\",\n    \"    if se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\" if abs(mean) < margin else \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(verdict, mean, 0.0, margin, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, mean, mean,\\n\",\n    \"                          abs(mean), n)\\n\",\n    \"    df_ = n - 1  # renamed from `df` -- that name is this notebook's DataFrame\\n\",\n    \"    t_lo = (mean + margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    t_hi = (mean - margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower = float(sps.t.sf(t_lo, df_))      # H0: diff <= -margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper = float(sps.t.cdf(t_hi, df_))     # H0: diff >= +margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)\\n\",\n    \"    crit = sps.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df_)\\n\",\n    \"    lo, hi = mean - crit * se, mean + crit * se\\n\",\n    \"    p_two = float(2 * sps.t.sf(abs(mean) / se, df_))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    if p_tost < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    elif p_two < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    else:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"INCONCLUSIVE\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    # smallest margin at which this data would have read EQUIVALENT\\n\",\n    \"    achieved = float(abs(mean) + crit * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return TostResult(verdict, mean, se, margin, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost,\\n\",\n    \"                      float(lo), float(hi), achieved, n)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def paired_bootstrap_se(diffs: np.ndarray, *, draws: int = N_BOOT,\\n\",\n    \"                        seed: int = RANDOM_SEED) -> float:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Bootstrap SE of the mean paired difference, used to invert R5's power sentence.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    if d.size < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\\n\",\n    \"    idx = rng.integers(0, d.size, size=(draws, d.size))\\n\",\n    \"    return float(np.std(d[idx].mean(axis=1), ddof=1))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def power_sentence(diffs: np.ndarray, *, label: str, power: float = 0.80,\\n\",\n    \"                   alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[str, float]:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"R5. Invert the paired bootstrap SE into the effect detectable at 80% power.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    se = paired_bootstrap_se(diffs)\\n\",\n    \"    n = int(np.isfinite(np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)).sum())\\n\",\n    \"    if not np.isfinite(se) or se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        why = \\\"n<2\\\" if n < 2 else \\\"bootstrap SE is exactly zero (degenerate outcome)\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, no detectable effect is \\\"\\n\",\n    \"                f\\\"computable: {why}\\\"), float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    mde = float((sps.norm.ppf(1 - alpha / 2) + sps.norm.ppf(power)) * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, a degradation of {mde:.4f} \\\"\\n\",\n    \"            f\\\"{label} would have been detected at power 0.80\\\"), mde\\n\",\n    \"# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"primary_deltas = [r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                  if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\" and r[\\\"window\\\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW\\n\",\n    \"                  and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"]\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"{PRIMARY_WINDOW} (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"{[round(v, 4) for v in primary_deltas]}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"t = tost(np.array(primary_deltas), MARGIN)\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\ntost(margin={MARGIN}): verdict={t.verdict}  mean_diff={t.diff:.4f}  \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"90% CI=[{t.ci90_low:.4f}, {t.ci90_high:.4f}]  p_tost={t.p_tost:.4g}  n={t.n}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"sent, mde = power_sentence(np.array(primary_deltas), label=\\\"TPR units\\\")\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\n{sent}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"check(\\\"mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows)\\\",\\n\",\n    \"      float(np.mean([r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                     if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\"\\n\",\n    \"                     and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"])),\\n\",\n    \"      \\\"m1_mean_delta_tpr_at_full_lesion\\\")\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"id\": \"9b02db86\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"## 5. Restricted-budget few-prompt axis: does the ordering track safety tuning?\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"For each lineage's **unlesioned** (`alpha=0.00`) primary-window arm, read off the mean AUROC of a probe fit on only `k` label-stratified items, for `k` in `BUDGETS`. {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"id\": \"942c861e\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"# Re-checking the numbers we already have: M1 recognition-with-headroom\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"This notebook is a Colab-runnable demo of the **evaluation artifact** `gen_art_evaluation_1` (\\\"Re-checking the numbers we already have\\\"), a **zero-GPU, zero-API re-adjudication** of a mechanistic-interpretability safety study on the **Qwen3-4B** lineage family: `L1` base, `L2` instruct, `L3` SafeRL (safe-completion), and `L4` a non-safety fine-tune used as a load-bearing control.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"Iteration 1 of that study reported that a harm-recognition probe's AUROC survives a representation *lesion* (an activation-steering ablation applied at strength `alpha` in `[0.00, 1.00]`) almost perfectly (~0.95-0.98 AUROC throughout). This artifact shows that AUROC was measured on an outcome that was **already at ceiling before the lesion**, so it could not have fallen in either direction. Re-expressed on an outcome **with headroom** -- TPR at a fixed, low false-positive rate -- the same activations reveal a **site dissociation**:\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"- **EARLY / prompt site** (reads the harmful *request*): the operating point is flat under the full lesion (`dTPR@1%FPR` +0.0007) -- recognition of the harmful request survives, as iteration 1 claimed.\\n\",\n    \"- **LATE / response site** (reads the model's *continuation*): the same statistic falls substantially (`dTPR@1%FPR` -0.1439) while AUROC there moves only -0.0137 -- about a **10.5x larger movement in the operating point than in the summary statistic that was reported**.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"This notebook also reproduces the TOST equivalence verdicts per lesion strength and the restricted-labelled-budget (`k` in `{16, 32, 64}`) AUROC ordering, which tracks safety tuning rather than raw capability: `Base ~ NonSafetyFT << Instruct < SafeRL`.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"## Run invariant\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"> The commissioned comparison and any metric built from it must read **ACTIVATIONS or WEIGHTS** of a single model. **Logit-only and text-only readouts are baselines, never the result.** Every row of every table carries a `READOUT_CLASS` field; no summary sentence may name a `BASELINE_ONLY` row as the answer.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"This is a **mechanistic-interpretability study of WHERE SAFETY LIVES** -- recognition of harm versus execution of a refusal -- not a jailbreak or attack-success-rate study. No attack-success rate appears as an outcome anywhere below; behavioural columns, where they appear, are only the ground truth an internal (activation-level) readout is validated against.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"**What this notebook does.** Because the raw activations/`.npz` files are not shipped with this demo, the notebook works from `mini_demo_data.json`: a 96-row curated subset of the artifact's own `results/m1_recognition_headroom.csv`, one row per (lineage x lesion-strength x window) arm plus paired lesion contrasts. It re-derives the M1 headline numbers from those stored rows and checks each one against the artifact's own `metrics_agg_reference`, printing MATCH/MISMATCH -- exactly the claim-checking style `eval.py` itself uses.\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n   \"execution_count\": 1,\n   \"id\": \"72ebc4f7\",\n   \"metadata\": {\n    \"execution\": {\n     \"iopub.execute_input\": \"2026-09-22T08:08:40.689129Z\",\n     \"iopub.status.busy\": \"2026-09-22T08:08:40.688990Z\",\n     \"iopub.status.idle\": \"2026-09-22T08:13:29.746017Z\",\n     \"shell.execute_reply\": \"2026-09-22T08:13:29.745401Z\"\n    }\n   },\n   \"outputs\": [],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"import subprocess, sys\\n\",\n    \"def _pip(*a): subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '-q', *a])\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy -- pre-installed on Colab, install locally to match\\n\",\n    \"# Colab's exact versions. \"'MATCH'\"\n      ]\n     },\n     \"execution_count\": 10,\n     \"metadata\": {},\n     \"output_type\": \"execute_result\"\n    }\n   ],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# --- copied verbatim from evalkit/stats.py -------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"@dataclass(frozen=True)\\n\",\n    \"class TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    verdict: str\\n\",\n    \"    diff: float\\n\",\n    \"    se: float\\n\",\n    \"    margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper: float\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_low: float\\n\",\n    \"    ci90_high: float\\n\",\n    \"    achieved_margin: float\\n\",\n    \"    n: int\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    def as_dict(self) -> dict:\\n\",\n    \"        return asdict(self)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def tost(diffs: np.ndarray, margin: float, *, alpha: float = 0.05) -> TostResult:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Two-one-sided-tests equivalence on a paired difference.\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    Returns EQUIVALENT only when the whole 1-2*alpha interval lies inside\\n\",\n    \"    (-margin, +margin). NOT_EQUIVALENT means the difference is itself\\n\",\n    \"    significantly non-zero; INCONCLUSIVE -- a real and expected verdict at these\\n\",\n    \"    sample sizes -- means neither, and is never to be reported as EQUIVALENT.\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    n = d.size\\n\",\n    \"    nan = float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    if n < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(\\\"INCONCLUSIVE_N_TOO_SMALL\\\", float(d.mean()) if n else nan,\\n\",\n    \"                          nan, margin, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, nan, n)\\n\",\n    \"    mean = float(d.mean())\\n\",\n    \"    se = float(d.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\\n\",\n    \"    if se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\" if abs(mean) < margin else \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return TostResult(verdict, mean, 0.0, margin, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, mean, mean,\\n\",\n    \"                          abs(mean), n)\\n\",\n    \"    df_ = n - 1  # renamed from `df` -- that name is this notebook's DataFrame\\n\",\n    \"    t_lo = (mean + margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    t_hi = (mean - margin) / se\\n\",\n    \"    p_lower = float(sps.t.sf(t_lo, df_))      # H0: diff <= -margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_upper = float(sps.t.cdf(t_hi, df_))     # H0: diff >= +margin\\n\",\n    \"    p_tost = max(p_lower, p_upper)\\n\",\n    \"    crit = sps.t.ppf(1 - alpha, df_)\\n\",\n    \"    lo, hi = mean - crit * se, mean + crit * se\\n\",\n    \"    p_two = float(2 * sps.t.sf(abs(mean) / se, df_))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"    if p_tost < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    elif p_two < alpha:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"NOT_EQUIVALENT\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    else:\\n\",\n    \"        verdict = \\\"INCONCLUSIVE\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    # smallest margin at which this data would have read EQUIVALENT\\n\",\n    \"    achieved = float(abs(mean) + crit * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return TostResult(verdict, mean, se, margin, p_lower, p_upper, p_tost,\\n\",\n    \"                      float(lo), float(hi), achieved, n)\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def paired_bootstrap_se(diffs: np.ndarray, *, draws: int = N_BOOT,\\n\",\n    \"                        seed: int = RANDOM_SEED) -> float:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"Bootstrap SE of the mean paired difference, used to invert R5's power sentence.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    d = np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)\\n\",\n    \"    d = d[np.isfinite(d)]\\n\",\n    \"    if d.size < 2:\\n\",\n    \"        return float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\\n\",\n    \"    idx = rng.integers(0, d.size, size=(draws, d.size))\\n\",\n    \"    return float(np.std(d[idx].mean(axis=1), ddof=1))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"def power_sentence(diffs: np.ndarray, *, label: str, power: float = 0.80,\\n\",\n    \"                   alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[str, float]:\\n\",\n    \"    \\\"\\\"\\\"R5. Invert the paired bootstrap SE into the effect detectable at 80% power.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\",\n    \"    se = paired_bootstrap_se(diffs)\\n\",\n    \"    n = int(np.isfinite(np.asarray(diffs, dtype=float)).sum())\\n\",\n    \"    if not np.isfinite(se) or se == 0.0:\\n\",\n    \"        why = \\\"n<2\\\" if n < 2 else \\\"bootstrap SE is exactly zero (degenerate outcome)\\\"\\n\",\n    \"        return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, no detectable effect is \\\"\\n\",\n    \"                f\\\"computable: {why}\\\"), float(\\\"nan\\\")\\n\",\n    \"    mde = float((sps.norm.ppf(1 - alpha / 2) + sps.norm.ppf(power)) * se)\\n\",\n    \"    return (f\\\"with this outcome and n = {n}, a degradation of {mde:.4f} \\\"\\n\",\n    \"            f\\\"{label} would have been detected at power 0.80\\\"), mde\\n\",\n    \"# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"primary_deltas = [r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                  if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\" and r[\\\"window\\\"] == PRIMARY_WINDOW\\n\",\n    \"                  and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"]\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"{PRIMARY_WINDOW} (primary window) full-lesion per-lineage TPR@1%FPR deltas: \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"{[round(v, 4) for v in primary_deltas]}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"t = tost(np.array(primary_deltas), MARGIN)\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\ntost(margin={MARGIN}): verdict={t.verdict}  mean_diff={t.diff:.4f}  \\\"\\n\",\n    \"      f\\\"90% CI=[{t.ci90_low:.4f}, {t.ci90_high:.4f}]  p_tost={t.p_tost:.4g}  n={t.n}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"sent, mde = power_sentence(np.array(primary_deltas), label=\\\"TPR units\\\")\\n\",\n    \"print(f\\\"\\\\n{sent}\\\")\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"check(\\\"mean delta TPR@1%FPR, all 8 full-lesion pairs (both windows)\\\",\\n\",\n    \"      float(np.mean([r[\\\"delta_tpr@1fpr\\\"] for r in lane_b_recs\\n\",\n    \"                     if r[\\\"metric\\\"] == \\\"M1.R4\\\"\\n\",\n    \"                     and r[\\\"alpha\\\"] == f\\\"{ALPHA_BASE}->{ALPHA_FULL}\\\"])),\\n\",\n    \"      \\\"m1_mean_delta_tpr_at_full_lesion\\\")\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"id\": \"9b02db86\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"## 5. Restricted-budget few-prompt axis: does the ordering track safety tuning?\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"For each lineage's **unlesioned** (`alpha=0.00`) primary-window arm, read off the mean AUROC of a probe fit on only `k` label-stratified items, for `k` in `BUDGETS`. This is the commissioned few-prompt axis (`evalkit/m1_recognition.py: restricted_budget_auroc`), de-saturating along *supervision* rather than along the lesion.
